description: A spectrogram: the same Fourier analysis drawn as a scrolling image, frequency up the screen and time across it, with level shown as colour.

params.text: Sets the gain on the input before analysis, from silence up to 12dB; it comes up at 6dB.
Stops and starts the buffering of fresh audio; switched off, the image stops scrolling.
Chooses one of fifteen window functions applied to the buffer before the transform, which trades frequency resolution against spectral leakage.
Chooses whether the frequency axis up the image is spaced linearly or logarithmically.
Sets the time constant of the averaging applied across successive analyses, 0 to 2500ms.
Sets how wide a band of neighbouring frequency bins is averaged together, from none up to 2.5 octaves.
Sets the lowest frequency drawn, 0Hz up to half the sample rate.
Sets the highest frequency drawn, 0Hz up to half the sample rate.
Tilts the drawn spectrum about 1kHz, -9 to +9dB per octave, to offset the fall of high frequency energy in music.

inputs.text: The audio to analyse; every channel of a polyphonic cable is summed into it, and 5V counts as full scale. The maker left this jack named TODO, which is what its tooltip reads.

notes: The module has no outputs. Audio patched in is analysed and drawn, and nothing comes back out.
The transform is fixed at 2048 samples and the image holds 512 columns of history; neither is adjustable, unlike the analyzer in this plugin.
The seven green words along the bottom of the display are the controls themselves: drag one up or down to change it.
menu: AC-coupled — passes the input through a DC blocker before the analysis
Color Map: Viridis, Cividis, Magma, Plasma, Inferno, Bone, Gray — chooses the colours level is drawn in
